newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen moving in tight range vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen moving in tight range vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar is likely to trade in a tight boxed range against the yen in Asia on Monday, as the market will remain focused on movements in the dollar/mark, dealers said.

The greenback was under slight profit-taking pressure versus the mark in early Asian trade after rising to an almost six-year high in Friday's New York trade, but sentiment for the greenback was expected to stay strong against the mark.
"The dollar/yen rate should stay in tight boxed ranges until trade figures are released later on during the week," a trust bank dealer in Tokyo said.
Japanese exporters and institutional investors are expected to sell on rallies, putting pressure on on the greenback above 114 yen, but its falls are likely to be limited at 112 yen.

"Looking at the fact the (the Finance Ministry's Eisuke) Sakakibara commented on the dollar when it was falling towards the 111-yen level last week, the market would be cautious if the dollar approached that level again," another dealer said.

Dealers were also cautiously watching the movements of the dollar/mark rate after the dollar rose as high as 1.7850 marks in New York on Friday after the German currency fell to 3.0 marks against sterling for the first time since October 1990.
